status.task:
Build a fully functional AI chatbot interface — a modern, production-ready ChatGPT-style chat app using React 18+, Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui conventions. The design follows the EaseMize UI aesthetic: ultra-clean, minimal, dark-mode-first with subtle warm gradients, rounded corners, and generous whitespace.

Layout & Structure:
- Full-height layout with a centered chat container (max-w-3xl or max-w-4xl).
- The app has two main views: (1) an empty state landing with a large centered headline "How Can I Help You" and the prompt input below it, and (2) an active chat view with a scrollable message thread and a fixed bottom input bar.
- A subtle radial gradient background: radial-gradient(125% 125% at 50% 101%, rgba(245,87,2,1) 10.5%, rgba(245,120,2,1) 16%, rgba(245,140,2,1) 17.5%, rgba(245,170,100,1) 25%, rgba(238,174,202,1) 40%, rgba(202,179,214,1) 65%, rgba(148,201,233,1) 100%) for the empty state; switch to a clean dark neutral background (#212121 or bg-background) for the active chat.
- Support both light and dark mode via CSS variables / next-themes.

Chat Interface:
- Message Bubbles: Distinct user (right-aligned, solid dark/light surface) and assistant (left-aligned, transparent/subtle border) bubbles. Rounded-2xl or rounded-3xl corners.
- Markdown Rendering: Full markdown support in assistant messages — headings, bold/italic, inline code, code blocks with syntax highlighting (use react-markdown + remark-gfm + a syntax highlighter like prism-react-renderer), tables, blockquotes, and lists.
- Real-Time Text Streaming: Simulate streaming token-by-token display for assistant responses. Show text appearing progressively with a smooth cursor or fade-in effect. Include a "typing" / "thinking" indicator (animated dots or pulsing dot) while the assistant is generating.
- Message Actions: Copy button on code blocks and assistant messages. Optional regenerate / thumbs up/down affordances.

Modern Prompt Input (Bottom Bar):
- A large, rounded-2xl input box (dark: bg-neutral-900, light: bg-white) with a subtle border, sitting at the bottom with safe padding.
- Placeholder text: "Ask anything..." or "How Can I Help You".
- Left actions: A circular "+" or paperclip icon button for image/file upload. On click, open a file picker supporting images (PNG, JPG, WEBP). Show image preview thumbnails inline above the input when attached (with remove option).
- Right actions: A circular send button (arrow-up icon) that appears/enables when there is text or attachments. Use a soft neutral or accent color.
- Model Selector: A small dropdown or segmented control inside the input bar showing the current model (e.g., "GPT 5.5") with an icon. Allow switching between model options.
- Effort/Mode Selector: A small toggle for effort levels (e.g., "Medium", "High") or reasoning mode.
- The input should auto-resize (max 6-8 lines) and support Shift+Enter for newlines.
- Keyboard shortcut: Cmd/Ctrl + Enter to send.

Chat History Management:
- A collapsible sidebar (left side, width ~260px) listing past conversations.
- Each history item shows a truncated title (first user message), timestamp, and a delete/edit icon on hover.
- "New Chat" button at the top of the sidebar (prominent, rounded).
- Clicking a history item loads that conversation thread into the main view.
- Persist chat history in localStorage or a simple in-memory store for demo purposes.

Empty State / Landing View:
- When no conversation is active, show the centered gradient background with the headline "How Can I Help You" in large, elegant typography (text-3xl to text-5xl, font-weight 500).
- Below the headline, render the same prompt input box, making it the focal point.
- Optional: suggested prompt chips below the input (e.g., "Write an email", "Summarize text", "Debug code") that auto-fill the input on click.

Header / Top Bar:
- Minimal top bar with a logo/brand mark on the left, the current model name in the center, and a theme toggle (sun/moon icon) on the right.
- When in an active chat, show the conversation title (editable) in the center.

Styling & UX Details:
- Use shadcn/ui primitives: Button, DropdownMenu, ScrollArea, Avatar, Tooltip, Separator.
- Tailwind spacing: generous padding (p-4 to p-6), gap-3 between messages.
- Typography: system font stack, clean sans-serif, text-sm for messages, text-xs for metadata.
- Smooth transitions: message appear animations (fade-in + slight translateY), input focus ring transitions.
- Scroll behavior: auto-scroll to bottom on new messages, with a "scroll to bottom" floating button if user scrolls up.
- Responsive: full-width on mobile, max-width container on desktop. Sidebar collapses to a drawer on mobile.

State Management:
- Use React hooks (useState, useRef, useEffect) for local state.
- Message state: array of {id, role: 'user' | 'assistant', content: string, attachments?: File[], timestamp, isStreaming?: boolean}.
- Simulate AI responses with a setTimeout/interval that streams words from a mock response array.

Accessibility:
- ARIA labels on all interactive elements.
- Keyboard-navigable sidebar and input.
- Focus visible states on buttons and inputs.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Tech Stack Requirements:
- Next.js 14+ App Router
- React 18+ (Server Components where possible, Client Components for interactive parts marked with "use client")
- TypeScript with strict types
- Tailwind CSS v3+
- shadcn/ui components (install via CLI: button, scroll-area, avatar, dropdown-menu, tooltip, separator)
- react-markdown + remark-gfm for markdown
- lucide-react for icons
- Optional: framer-motion for smooth message entrance animations

Deliverable: A single, self-contained Next.js page (or split into logical components: ChatLayout, MessageList, PromptInput, ChatSidebar, EmptyState) that runs out of the box with npm run dev. All code must be production-quality, fully typed, and follow shadcn/ui conventions (cn() utility, consistent class naming).

IMPORTANT: Scaffold the Next.js app yourself (create package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.mjs, tailwind.config.ts, postcss.config.js), install dependencies via npm, write all components, run the build, start the dev server, and verify the UI using browser tools (browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_screenshot). Verify that the empty state renders, a message can be sent, streaming/markdown works, and provide a screenshot of the result. Do not ask for clarification and do not finish until real files exist and the app runs.

steps.description: Initialize the Next.js project structure, creating `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.mjs`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `postcss.config.mjs`, and the base folder hierarchy (`app`, `components`, `lib`, `public`).
Install all required dependencies (Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MD libraries, icons, shadcn deps, and framer-motion).
Configure `app/globals.css` with the EaseMize aesthetic (radial gradients, dark mode CSS variables) and update `tailwind.config.ts` to include the correct paths and theme extensions.

Create `lib/utils.ts` and the necessary shadcn/ui primitive components (`button`, `scroll-area`, `avatar`, `dropdown-menu`, `tooltip`, `separator`, `input`, `textarea`) in the `components/ui` directory.

Build the specialized chat components (`ChatSidebar`, `ChatHeader`, `PromptInput`, `MessageList`, `EmptyState`) with full TypeScript types and the requested UI/UX features (attachments, auto-resize, markdown).
Implement the main application logic in `app/page.tsx`, integrating state management (localStorage, streaming simulation), theme provider, and the responsive layout.
Run `npm run build` to verify the code compiles successfully and there are no TypeScript or dependency errors.
Start the development server in the background with logging.
Navigate to the application in the browser and verify the empty state renders correctly with the gradient background and prompt input.
Send a test message via the browser to trigger the active chat state, verify the streaming response and markdown rendering, and take a final screenshot.
